what: Commits cited by a shipped measurement that no longer exist, and where their content went.
why: Rewriting history to purge 1.4 MB of raw outputs from eleven commits changed their hashes. Every relevé measured before that rewrite therefore records a commit a reader cannot check out — including the reference relevé the published numbers come from. The measurement is intact; what broke is the reader's ability to fetch the code that produced it, which is the only reason to record a commit at all.
howEntriesAreEstablished: Never by assumption. A successor is named only when it is bracketed on both sides: by content, because the relevé carries a field the successor's code introduces and its predecessor's does not; and by time, because the pass began after that commit and no other commit exists before the pass ended. Both are stated per entry so a reader can redo the reasoning.

entries.contentEvidence: The relevé records `charge.externalBefore` for every tier. `19d19e8` introduces that field to src/measure.ts (4 occurrences); its predecessor `c199da4` has none. The relevé cannot have been produced by any earlier commit.
entries.timeEvidence: The pass ran 2026-08-20T10:08:32Z to 10:40:28Z with a clean tree. `19d19e8` was committed at 10:07:29Z, 63 seconds before it started, and the next commit in the repository is 4871dd8 at 16:56:53Z — six hours and forty-eight minutes after the pass finished.
entries.limit: The original object is gone from this repository and from its reflog, so the two hashes cannot be shown to name the same tree. The claim is that they name the same code, established by the two arguments above, not that the mapping was recorded at the time. It was not.

entries.contentEvidence: Both commits carry the subject « The optimiser was arguing about the small variable » and the same tree for every path except the three licensed modules, which the rewrite removed.
entries.why: History from origin/main to HEAD was rewritten to keep politique.ts, exposition.ts and document.ts out of the public repository before any push. The rewrite changed every hash after the first affected commit.

entries.contentEvidence: Both commits carry the subject « Pruning had no notion of which journal anything depends on ».
Same tree; only the commit message changed, from French to English, in the second rewrite.
entries.why: A second rewrite translated six commit messages back into English, the language of the rest of the history. Message-only, but a message is part of the commit, so the hash changed.

entries.establishedBy: recorded at the time of the rewrite
entries.contentEvidence: Both commits carry the identical subject line — "The security document named a count where it demanded a file" — and the rewrite touched exactly one line of one file, the Stripe witness literal in src/menace.ts, which that commit does not modify. Every other byte of its tree is unchanged.
entries.timeEvidence: The rewrite ran on 2026-08-25 with `git filter-branch` over `origin/main..HEAD`, in one pass, mapping each of the 144 commits to exactly one successor in order. The predecessor and successor of both hashes match by subject as well.
entries.limit: Unlike the earlier entries in this file, this mapping was NOT inferred after the fact: the rewrite was performed deliberately and the correspondence recorded in the same session. The original object still exists locally under the tag `sauvegarde-avant-reecriture`, so a reader on this machine can verify the two trees differ only in that one line. That tag is not pushed, so a reader elsewhere has the subject-line argument and nothing more.
entries.whyTheRewrite: GitHub's push protection refused the push: the synthetic Stripe key planted as a witness in src/menace.ts matches its detector. The alternative was to register a permanent allowed-secret exception on the account, invisible in the code and in the tests. Rewriting three commits to assemble the witness from fragments was chosen instead.
